competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move. Supported STIR contracts use exchange DV01 and currency conversion; historical rows without that stamp keep the legacy duration-one vintage and are not silently restated. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

quarterly.coverage_note: Official StatCan sector Energy. Bank of Canada Staff Analytical Paper 2026-46 groups NAICS 211 oil and gas extraction, 2121 coal mining, and 22 utilities. This is the direct quarterly energy producer-price aggregate.
quarterly.label: Energy

import_price_measure.documentation: RMPI table 18-10-0268-01 prices raw materials purchased by Canadian manufacturers and includes domestically produced materials. It is not an import price index. Prima's import node in Staff Analytical Paper 2026-47 is not identified with RMPI. No import-price cube is pinned here, so imported cost pressure is not labeled.

other_sectors.coverage_note: Official StatCan sector Non-Energy. SAP 2026-46 defines it as selected agriculture, forestry, fishing, metal-ore mining, and non-metallic mineral mining. It is not IPPI excluding energy and it is not a residual of all non-energy producer prices.
other_sectors.label: Non-Energy

other_sectors.coverage_note: Official StatCan sector Goods. SAP 2026-46 includes manufacturing, whose price source is total IPPI vector 1230995983 (energy and petroleum products included), plus selected residential and non-residential building construction. It is not a non-energy goods index and must not be added to the Energy sector.
other_sectors.label: Goods

other_sectors.coverage_note: Official StatCan sector Services. SAP 2026-46 covers selected wholesale, retail, rail freight, truck transportation, couriers, and commercial machinery rental and leasing. Coverage is incomplete and the index starts later than the other three sectors. This is an observed sector price, not an estimated pass-through elasticity.
other_sectors.label: Services

sentences.do_not_sum: Do not add Energy to Non-Energy, Goods, or Services. They are separate analytical aggregates. Goods includes total IPPI, so it is not a non-energy transmission measure and it is not added to the Energy sector.
sentences.headline_versus_ex_energy: Monthly IPPI excluding energy is +0.28% and scores production-network pressure as STABLE. Headline IPPI, which includes energy, is +1.962% month over month. IPPI energy and petroleum products are +12.084% month over month. Quarterly Energy sector PPI is +19.847% q/q in 2026-Q2, released 2026-10-09T08:30. Data age is 34 days after that release. That quarterly energy move is not added to the production-network channel. Headline IPPI and the Energy sector can move when IPPI excluding energy does not. The scored production-network channel uses only the monthly ex-energy index.
sentences.no_pass_through_model: No pass-through elasticity is estimated. These are separate observed price changes, not a structural Prima decomposition and not a reproduction of the Bank of Canada's model.
sentences.raw_materials: Monthly RMPI excluding crude energy is -0.435% and scores the stored imported_pressure channel as FALLING. This is StatCan's raw-materials price index for purchases by Canadian manufacturers, including domestically produced materials. It is not an import-price index. RMPI crude energy is +14.42% month over month and is not part of that channel. No import-price series is pinned, so imported cost pressure is not labeled.
sentences.revision: Each quarterly release can revise the previous two quarters. Weight updates revise the index back to the start of the new weight reference year. This feed stores the latest vintage only, not a real-time history. Observable release vintages in this response: 1. Back history published on the first public release (2026-10-09) was not observable in earlier quarters. A scored change is not proposed: the sample is not a real-time track record, the indexes are quarterly, and no Prima weights or elasticities are published.
sentences.score_guard: The quarterly sector layer is shadow-only. It is not in the direction, strength, or net vote, and it does not replace monthly IPPI excluding energy or RMPI excluding crude energy.
sentences.sensitivity: Quarterly q/q readings are not classified with the monthly IPPI or RMPI bands. The monthly bands are unchanged, and these quarterly changes are not in the scored vote. Proposed scored change: none.

method.note: Live authorities remain canonical. This artifact is a compact research snapshot. US, Australia, ECB FX, and CFTC positioning remain packet-level preflight. A stale Canadian benchmark yield stays visible on CA_rates and does not by itself mark the packet stale. CA-dependent expressions and existing-book positions that depend on that leg fail closed. Canadian benchmark freshness uses the Canadian business-day calendar and a one-session publication lag. NZ and Japan are not required_for_trader_preflight; a blocked RBNZ source or a Japan holiday-calendar print stays visible on that source and does not by itself mark the packet stale. NZ-dependent and JP-dependent expressions still fail closed. The official RBNZ B2 XLSX is tried first, including a browser-TLS retry, then the official RBNZ B2 HTML table. No vendor or media substitute is used. Japan JGB freshness uses the Tokyo business-day calendar and a one-session publication lag. Euro-area Bund (Germany) and Japan JGB cash curves remain six-economy rate legs. Cross-country spreads use exact common observation dates only. Policy-path context uses official overnight benchmarks plus public money-market data. The required tradable paper rates universe remains SOFR via CME SR3, CORRA via MX CRA, and AONIA via ASX IB. TONA is included when JPX OSE 3M settlements pass identity checks. CME ESR final settlements are collected for research; the €STR curve stays observe_only; Eurex FST3 is not a mark. Official government zero/forward curves are supplemental bond-curve inputs and are not required to manufacture a swap curve. Euro-area sovereign fragmentation (IT/FR/ES vs Bund) is market context, never an EA temperature input. Housing context is collected for the US, Canada and Australia from free maintained public sources: FHFA/Census/Fed/Freddie Mac via FRED for the US, Statistics Canada/CMHC/Bank of Canada for Canada, and ABS/RBA for Australia. EA/JP housing is omitted until an official/free source meets the contract. CFTC TFF supplies trader-class ownership/crowding context and can mark the packet stale. CME's public volume/open-interest service is a supplemental overlay and does not flip packet status. No historical warehouse is written to GitHub or Supabase.

contracts_eus.ds_header: Euro Short-Term Rate (€STR) - Three-Month Single Contract Basis Spread Futures
contracts_eus.economics_source: CME SER-9059 Exhibit 1, Rulebook Chapter 481: the quote is the Euribor-minus-€STR basis in percent per annum, €25 per basis point; minimum price increment 0.0025 index points equals €6.25. Final settlement assigns the same named-month ESR future at 100 minus the Euribor fixing plus the EUS final settlement.
contracts_eus.paper_blocker: A long EUS final settlement assigns a long ESR future of the same named month. ESR remains observe_only, so EUS is not opened as a paper position.
contracts_eus.period_note: SER-9059 prices the spread over the same interest period as the named-month Euribor and compounded €STR. The settlement file itself does not reprint those fixing dates. Final settlement assigns ESR, it does not leave an open spread.
contracts_eus.quote_convention: direct basis settlement in index points, not 100 minus a rate

contracts_eus.economics_source: CME SER-9059 Exhibit 1, Rulebook Chapter 481: the quote is the Euribor-minus-€STR basis in percent per annum, €25 per basis point; minimum price increment 0.0025 index points equals €6.25. Final settlement assigns the same named-month ESR future at 100 minus the Euribor fixing plus the EUS final settlement.
contracts_eus.paper_blocker: A long EUS final settlement assigns a long ESR future of the same named month. ESR remains observe_only, so EUS is not opened as a paper position.
contracts_eus.period_note: SER-9059 prices the spread over the same interest period as the named-month Euribor and compounded €STR. The settlement file itself does not reprint those fixing dates. Final settlement assigns ESR, it does not leave an open spread.
contracts_eus.quote_convention: direct basis settlement in index points, not 100 minus a rate

terminal.compounding_formula: R = [product_i (1 + di/360 * ri/100) - 1] * (360/D) * 100, di = calendar days to the next TARGET business day
terminal.spec_source: CME Rulebook Chapter 480; named month starts the reference quarter

# Trader Room Research Method

## Purpose

This is the durable research discipline every Trader Room advocate must apply before its archetypal bias. It captures the reusable empirical method retained from Market Watch's review of Bob Elliott / Nonconsensus and David Cervantes / Pinebrook research. Adopt the process, not either author's current conclusions, positions, forecasts, or trade calls. Live evidence and Market Watch analysis control.

## Required method

## Context-before-screen rule

The idea-building order is mandatory: **context -> what changed -> what is priced -> historical comparison -> discrepancy -> expression -> sizing**. A percentile, z-score, historical spread extreme or correlation break is a discovery signal, never the trade thesis.

Before using a statistical screen, reconstruct how the market got to the current price. Identify the major price move over multiple horizons, the events/information/flows that drove it, and what was already known versus genuinely new. For rates, begin with the observable policy path (OIS/STIR/overnight benchmark) before interpreting sovereign yields or cross-country spreads.

Bob Elliott / Nonconsensus-style idea construction is the default empirical sequence: state the causal mechanism, identify the priced assumption, locate comparable historical episodes, quantify what happened next, then explain why today's regime is similar **and** structurally different. David Cervantes / Pinebrook-style math is then used to test the narrative: decomposition, distributions, cross-market consistency, holder/flow context and forward outcomes. Statistics refine conviction, entry and size after the context survives.

1. **Start with a causal question.** State the mechanism being tested and convert the narrative into measurable claims. Separate state from change, level from marginal move, and known information from genuinely new information.
2. **Normalize correctly.** Use the economically relevant denominator, ratio, spread, growth rate, risk adjustment, tenor, benchmark, or comparison set. Compare like with like.
3. **Establish the historical reference distribution.** Where data permits, use mean/median, range, percentiles, standard deviations or z-scores, rolling windows, and forward outcomes after comparable states. Use multiple horizons and identify regime breaks rather than blindly pooling history.
4. **Decompose aggregates.** Break headline measures and market prices into the components or accounting channels that can produce them. Use decomposition to identify why an aggregate moved; do not confuse an identity with causality.
5. **Triangulate.** Important conclusions should survive multiple independent datasets or measurement approaches when practical. Preserve disagreement between hard data, surveys, market measures, flows, physical data, and micro evidence rather than averaging conflicts away.
6. **Make market expectations explicit.** Never stop at strong/weak data. Ask what current pricing already requires to be true. Use observable implied measures where available; otherwise state the assumptions being backsolved. The opportunity is usually the gap between fundamentals and pricing, not the absolute level of the data.
7. **Build a discrepancy map.** Test data vs consensus, fundamentals vs market pricing, market vs market, current level vs historical distribution, headline vs components, and narrative vs hard/physical data. A discrepancy is not a trade without a plausible closing mechanism.
8. **Separate fundamentals from flow and plumbing.** Test whether price action is better explained by positioning, leverage, liquidation, dealer balance sheet, hedging, intervention, month-end, CTA/systematic flow, liquidity, or other non-fundamental mechanics before treating it as new macro information.
9. **Define falsifiers before sizing.** State observations that would weaken or invalidate the causal mechanism. Distinguish wrong thesis from right thesis/wrong timing. Reassess horizon and carry when the mechanism remains intact but timing slips.
10. **Express the trade where the mispricing lives.** Prefer the tenor, curve, cross-country, cross-asset, sector, spot pair, or option structure that most directly owns the discrepancy. Risk-match comparisons. Use statistical stretch to improve entry/sizing after the fundamental discrepancy is established, not instead of it.

## David Cervantes risk and pricing discipline

- Separate the strategic regime from the tactical trade; state both horizons.
- Mean reversion is a yardstick, not a signal. Statistical stretch requires a catalyst, weakening mechanism, or independent evidence.
- Models define plausible ranges, not exact entries. Do not manufacture precision from a z-score or decomposition.
- Triangulate models and then apply economic judgment; no single framework gets veto power.
- Let price decomposition reveal what the market currently cares about rather than assuming a fixed reaction function.
- Treat market prices as anticipatory and realized macro data as later confirmation; explicitly model the lag from shock to market response to realized data.
- Treat latent/model-estimated components such as term premium as useful proxies, not directly observable physical truths.
- Respect tenor-specific ownership and preferred habitat. Do not read a 30Y move automatically as the same signal as a 10Y move.
- Holder composition changes the risk distribution. Separate leveraged/mark-to-market behavior from price-insensitive or buy-and-hold ownership.
- Known information needs a new transmission mechanism to explain a new move.

## Minimum evidence test for a material trade

When data availability permits, an advocate should be able to identify: causal mechanism; current state and direction; normalization; historical reference; market-implied assumption; precise discrepancy; independent triangulation; catalyst/transmission path; fundamental invalidation; and why the chosen expression owns the edge.

## Guardrails

Do not data-mine transformations until one confirms the desired conclusion. Do not treat statistical extremes as guaranteed mean reversion. Do not use historical analogs without identifying structural differences. Do not infer causality from correlation alone. Preserve data vintages when they affect what was knowable. Missing evidence lowers confidence; it is never permission to guess.

## ChatGPT PM research memory

The ChatGPT PM seat persists hypotheses, evidence assessments, and a trading-edge profile in Git (`data/trading/pm/chatgpt/research/`). That store follows the context-before-screen discipline here but is **not** a substitute for frozen Trader Room packets or for booking trades. Cold-start retrieval, ticket schema, and the split from `[chatgpt-pm-decision]` are in [`docs/CHATGPT_RESEARCH_MEMORY_V1.md`](CHATGPT_RESEARCH_MEMORY_V1.md).
